content: 1. Lopinavir is contraindicated in cases where it significantly alters the metabolism of drugs via the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Close monitoring is required when lopinavir decreases the effects of exenatide injectable solution. Reports indicate hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Caution is advised. 2. Lopinavir decreases the effects of exenatide injectable suspension. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. Monitor closely. 3. Lopinavir and ezogabine may increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Ezogabine has been associated with slight and transient QT prolongation, particularly at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is co-administered with agents known to prolong the QT interval. 4. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. If fedratinib must be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase the fedratinib dose to 300 mg/day for 2 weeks, then to 400 mg/day as tolerated. 5. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of felbamate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 6. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of felodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal formulations) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 8. Lopinavir decreases the level or effect of fexinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Both fexinidazole and lopinavir increase the QTc interval, necessitating caution. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 9. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Lopinavir and fingolimod both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 11. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Flibanserin co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 12. Fluconazole increases the level or effect of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Fludrocortisone decreases the level or effect of lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of flunisolide (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Lopinavir increases the level of flurazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose. 16. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of fluticasone furoate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid exposure. Monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type symptoms. 17. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of fluticasone (inhaled and intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects. 18. Fluvoxamine increases the level or effect of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Fosamprenavir increases the level or effect of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and vice versa. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 20. Fosaprepitant increases the level or effect of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and vice versa. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Fosphenytoin decreases the level or effect of lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of fostamatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (fostamatinib's major active metabolite). Monitor for toxicities that may require dose reduction. 23. Lopinavir and fostemsavir both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 24. Lopinavir and ganaxolone interactions are minor, with no clinically significant changes in ganaxolone exposures expected when co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 25. Lopinavir increases the level of gefitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. 26. Lopinavir and gemifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 27. Lopinavir and gemtuzumab both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Both drugs increase the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. 29. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Both drugs increase the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring for adverse effects if co-administration is unavoidable. 30. Lopinavir and givinostat both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or changes from baseline by more than 60 ms. 31. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Both drugs increase the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring for QTc prolongation if co-administration is unavoidable. 32. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 33. Lopinavir decreases the effects of glimepiride by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate close monitoring. 34. Lopinavir may increase or decrease the levels of glipizide. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate close monitoring. 35. Lopinavir decreases the effects of glyburide. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate close monitoring. 36. Goserelin increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the increased risk of torsades de pointes. 37. Lopinavir and granisetron both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 38. Grapefruit increases the level or effect of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Griseofulvin decreases the level or effect of lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. FDA-approved labeling for extended-release guanfacine recommends halving the dose when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 41. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 42. Histrelin increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs due to the increased risk of torsades de pointes. 43. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 44. Hydrocortisone decreases the level or effect of lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Lopinavir and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 46. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 47. Lopinavir and hydroxyzine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 48. Lopinavir increases the level of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 49. Idelalisib increases the level or effect of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 50. Lopinavir decreases the level or effect of ifosfamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, reducing its efficacy. 51. Iloperidone increases the level of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 52. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 53. Lopinavir and indacaterol (inhaled) both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs known to prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 54. Indinavir increases the level or effect of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and vice versa. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs.
